items.title: A nonsingular Pfaff one-form and its horizontal paths

references.title: Ko Honda, Differential Geometry Course Notes, §33.2, full 84-page lecture notes
Leonard Tomczak, notes for Jack Smith, Differential Geometry, §§2.5 and 6.2, full lecture notes

items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be open, $n\ge1$, with coordinates $(x_1,\ldots,x_n,z)$. For $k\in\{1,2\}$, a $C^k$ one-form on $U$ is a field of linear functionals on tangent vectors of the form $\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i(x,z)\,dx_i+b(x,z)\,dz$, where every coefficient is $k$ times continuously differentiable. At $q\in U$, it acts by $\omega_q(u_1,\ldots,u_n,w)=\sum_i a_i(q)u_i+b(q)w$. It is nonsingular on $U$ when $\omega_q\ne0$ for every $q$; then $H_q:=\ker\omega_q$ is an $n$-dimensional subspace of $T_qU\cong\mathbb R^{n+1}$.

For a $C^1$ scalar function $S:W\to\mathbb R$ on an open $W\subseteq U$, its differential is the one-form defined by

$$dS_q(v):=DS(q)v=\sum_{i=1}^n\partial_{x_i}S(q)u_i+\partial_zS(q)w,\qquad v=(u_1,\ldots,u_n,w)\in T_qW.$$

In particular, if $S\in C^2(W)$, then $dS$ is a $C^1$ one-form.

For one-forms $\alpha,\beta$, their exterior product is the alternating two-form $(\alpha\wedge\beta)(u,v)=\alpha(u)\beta(v)-\alpha(v)\beta(u)$. For a one-form $\alpha$ and a two-form $\sigma$, $(\alpha\wedge\sigma)(u,v,w)=\alpha(u)\sigma(v,w)-\alpha(v)\sigma(u,w)+\alpha(w)\sigma(u,v)$. For a $C^1$ one-form $\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\,dx_i+b\,dz$, its exterior derivative is the continuous two-form

$$d\omega=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}(\partial_i a_j-\partial_j a_i)\,dx_i\wedge dx_j+\sum_{i=1}^n(\partial_i b-\partial_z a_i)\,dx_i\wedge dz.$$

When $\omega$ is $C^2$, the coefficients of $d\omega$ are $C^1$.

For a $C^2$ one-form on this page, the codimension-one Pfaff condition means the pointwise equation $\omega\wedge d\omega=0$.

A piecewise-$C^1$ path is a continuous $\gamma:[s_0,s_1]\to U$ with $s_0\le s_1$ and admitting a finite partition on each closed subinterval of which it is $C^1$. It is $\omega$-horizontal when $\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))=0$ on the interior of each such subinterval. Endpoints where a derivative is one-sided are included by continuity. For an open $V\subseteq U$, $p$ is horizontally reachable from $q$ within $V$ if a horizontal path in $V$ joins $q$ to $p$. Both signs of time and finite concatenations are allowed by this definition.

On a neighborhood $W$, an integrating factor for $\omega$ is a nowhere-zero $\mu\in C^1(W)$ for which $\mu\omega=dS$ for some $S\in C^2(W)$ with $dS$ nowhere zero. This definition is local; it asserts neither a global potential on $U$ nor a physical identification or calibration of $S$.

items.title: Local flows by a contraction argument

references.title: Ko Honda, Differential Geometry Course Notes, §33.1, full 84-page lecture notes
Leonard Tomczak, notes for Jack Smith, Differential Geometry, §§5.1 and 6.3, full lecture notes

items.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, $m\ge1$, let $X:U\to\mathbb R^m$ have continuous first partial derivatives, and fix $q_0\in U$. There are $r,\delta>0$ and a map $\phi:[-\delta,\delta]\times\overline B(q_0,r/2)\to\overline B(q_0,r)$ such that for each $p\in\overline B(q_0,r/2)$, $t\mapsto\phi(t,p)$ is $C^1$, satisfies $\phi(0,p)=p$ and $\partial_t\phi(t,p)=X(\phi(t,p))$ on $(-\delta,\delta)$, and is the unique such solution that stays in $\overline B(q_0,r)$. The dependence on the initial point is locally Lipschitz, and the local flow law $\phi(t,\phi(s,p))=\phi(t+s,p)$ holds whenever the displayed maps are defined in the chosen neighborhood.

items.title: Variational equations and commuting local flows

references.title: Ko Honda, Differential Geometry Course Notes, §33.1, full 84-page lecture notes
Pavel Etingof, Lie groups and Lie algebras, arXiv:2201.09397v5, §10.1, Theorem 10.6 and proof, pp. 55–57

items.statement: Let $X$ be a $C^2$ vector field on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, where $C^2$ means that total derivatives through order two exist and are continuous. Its local flow $\phi_X^t(q)$ from [[lem-tdmath-local-contraction-flow]] is $C^2$ jointly in $(t,q)$, and $J(t,q):=D_q\phi_X^t(q)$ satisfies $\partial_tJ=DX(\phi_X^t(q))J$ and $J(0,q)=I$. For two such fields define their bracket by $[X,Y](q):=DY(q)X(q)-DX(q)Y(q)$. If $[X,Y]=0$ on a neighborhood and all local maps stay there, then $D_q\phi_X^t(q)Y(q)=Y(\phi_X^t(q))$ and their local flows commute: $\phi_X^t\circ\phi_Y^s=\phi_Y^s\circ\phi_X^t$ whenever both sides are defined.

items.title: An exact nonzero multiple satisfies the Pfaff condition

references.title: Ko Honda, Differential Geometry Course Notes, §33.2, full 84-page lecture notes

items.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ be open. Let $\omega$ be a $C^1$ one-form on $U$, $\mu\in C^1(U)$ nowhere zero, and $S\in C^2(U)$ with $dS=\mu\omega$. Then $\omega\wedge d\omega=0$ on $U$.

items.title: The local nonsingular codimension-one Pfaff–Frobenius theorem

references.title: Ko Honda, Differential Geometry Course Notes, §§33.1–33.2, full 84-page lecture notes
Pavel Etingof, Lie groups and Lie algebras, arXiv:2201.09397v5, §10.1, Theorem 10.6 and proof, pp. 55–57

items.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $n\ge1$, be open and let $\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i dx_i+b dz$ be a $C^2$ one-form with $\omega_{q_0}\ne0$ at $q_0\in U$. Relabel coordinates so one coefficient $b$ is nonzero at $q_0$ and shrink to a neighborhood where it stays nonzero. The following conditions, both local at $q_0$, are equivalent: (i) there is a neighborhood $U_0$ of $q_0$ on which $\omega\wedge d\omega=0$; (ii) there is a neighborhood $W$ of $q_0$ and $\mu\in C^1(W)$ nowhere zero and $S\in C^2(W)$ with $dS=\mu\omega$ on $W$. The theorem gives no global exactness or thermodynamic calibration.

items.title: Horizontal orbits under local first integrals have empty interior
items.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $n\ge1$, be open, and let $\omega$ be a nowhere-zero $C^2$ one-form, with the horizontal paths of [[def-tdmath-one-form-and-horizontal-path]]. Assume that every point has a neighborhood $W$ with $S\in C^2(W)$ and nowhere-zero $\mu\in C^1(W)$ satisfying $dS=\mu\omega$. For every $q\in U$, its horizontal reachability class in $U$ is contained in a countable union of compact subsets of $U$ with empty interior. Consequently every nonempty open $V\subseteq U$ contains a point not horizontally reachable from $q$ by any horizontal path in $U$. In particular, if $q\in V$, that point is not reachable by a path contained in $V$. No global first integral or choice axiom is assumed.

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie groups and Lie algebras, arXiv:2201.09397v5, §10.1, Lemma 10.3 and Theorem 10.6, pp. 54–57

items.title: Local horizontal inaccessibility and Pfaff integrability
items.statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $n\ge1$, be open and let $\omega$ be a nowhere-zero $C^2$ one-form. Suppose horizontal paths and local reachability are as in [[def-tdmath-one-form-and-horizontal-path]]. The following are equivalent: (a) for every $q\in U$ and every open neighborhood $V$ of $q$ contained in $U$, some $p\in V$ is not horizontally reachable from $q$ by a path contained in $V$; (b) every $q\in U$ has a neighborhood $W$ and $\mu\in C^1(W)$ nowhere zero, $S\in C^2(W)$ with $dS=\mu\omega$. Both conditions are local. This is a mathematical theorem about the declared horizontal-path relation; identifying that relation with physical adiabatic processes is an additional modeling assumption.

references.title: Ko Honda, Differential Geometry Course Notes, §33 and §33.2, full 84-page lecture notes

items.title: A two-dimensional Pfaff form with a global integrating factor

references.title: Ko Honda, Differential Geometry Course Notes, §33, full lecture notes

items.statement: On $\mathbb R^2$ with coordinates $(x,y)$, let $\omega=dy+y\,dx$. It is a smooth nowhere-zero one-form because its $dy$ coefficient is $1$. The functions $\mu(x,y)=e^x$ and $S(x,y)=e^xy$ satisfy $\mu>0$ and $dS=\mu\omega$ globally.

items.statement: Every nowhere-zero $C^2$ one-form on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ has a nonzero local integrating factor making it exact.

items.title: A closed one-form on the punctured plane with nonzero period

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis II, §§9.2.11 and 9.3.3, full-text line-integral chapter

items.statement: Every closed $C^1$ one-form on every connected open domain in $\mathbb R^2$ is globally exact.
